name: feature_parsimony_heuristic
hypothesis: Listeners interpret referring expressions using a non-Bayesian feature-parsimony heuristic rather than recursive Theory of Mind. When hearing a feature word, listeners select among the objects of which the word is literally true by penalizing objects that possess superfluous unmentioned features, exponentially preferring the most minimal referent. On trials without an informative word, listeners choose uniformly among available objects.

name: singleton_isolation_listener
hypothesis: Listeners exhibit an isolation preference, placing high prior expectation on contextually unique singletons over objects with identical duplicates in the display. On displays containing two identical objects and one singleton where a shared feature is heard, this predicts listeners will predominantly choose the singleton, whereas RSA depth-2 predicts listeners will choose the duplicate objects because a speaker intending the singleton would have used its unique feature.

name: discriminative_alternative_speaker
hypothesis: Speakers experience a communicative penalty when choosing an ambiguous word if a uniquely distinguishing word for their intended referent was available in the visual context. Pragmatic listeners invert this speaker, recognizing that a speaker who uses an ambiguous word either had no distinguishing alternative or faced production costs, driving pragmatic reference resolution.

name: rsa_l2_shared_prior
hypothesis: Listeners reason at depth 2 (inverting a speaker who simulates a pragmatic listener) while treating object salience—driven by feature count and familiarization base rates—as common knowledge across all levels of recursion. By sharing the salience prior among the literal listener, both simulated speakers, and the pragmatic listener (and defaulting to this prior on prior trials), the model accounts for contextual object preferences and prior elicitation while preserving depth-2 pragmatic implicature. Compared to rsa_l2, recursion depth remains at L2, two parameters (w_features and w_familiar) are added to form the shared salience prior via softmax, the object prior at every level (L0, S1, S2, and L2) changes from uniform to this salience prior, and choices on prior trials evaluate to this prior rather than uniform guessing.

name: rsa_l2_salience
hypothesis: We refine rsa_l2 by incorporating an asymmetric object salience prior (taking the salience prior component from rsa_l1_salience) at the depth-2 pragmatic listener level: listeners combine depth-2 recursive pragmatic reasoning with a subjective salience prior over referents based on feature counts and familiarization base rates, while modeling simulated lower-level agents as reasoning with uniform object priors. This allows listeners to capture contextual exposure and perceptual biases—and predict non-uniform choices on uninformative prior trials—without assuming that lower-level literal and pragmatic reasoning is biased by referent salience. Compared to rsa_l2, recursion depth remains at L2, two parameters (w_features and w_familiar) are added to construct the salience prior, the prior enters the top-level speaker simulation S2 in L2 as a prior over referents (while L0 and S1 retain uniform object priors), and choices on prior trials evaluate to this salience prior rather than uniform guessing.

hypothesis: We refine rsa_l1_shared_prior by increasing listener reasoning to depth 2: listeners invert a speaker who simulates a depth-1 pragmatic listener rather than a literal listener, while maintaining the shared salience prior across all levels of recursive reasoning. This higher-order recursive inference allows listeners to resolve complex scalar implicatures that depth-1 reasoning fails to disambiguate, while preserving the grounding of referential expectations in mutual perceptual and familiarization salience. Differences from rsa_l1_shared_prior: - Recursion depth: choice_probs calls L2 instead of L1. - Agent hierarchy: introduces a pragmatic speaker S2 who anticipates pragmatic listener L1, and an L2 listener who inverts S2, with the shared salience prior used at all levels (L0, S1, L1, S2, L2). - Parameters: no parameters added or removed (retains alpha, w_features, w_familiar, and lapse).

name: rsa_l1_singleton_shared_prior
hypothesis: We refine rsa_l1_shared_prior by incorporating an isolation preference for contextually unique singletons (taking the singleton isolation component from singleton_isolation_listener) into the shared object prior: listeners and the speakers they model treat unique singletons lacking identical duplicates in the visual display as salient referents alongside familiar and feature-sparse objects. This perceptual isolation bias elevates singletons over identical duplicate objects when resolving ambiguous expressions or selecting objects on uninformative prior trials, while preserving mutual salience grounding and pragmatic implicature. Compared to rsa_l1_shared_prior, recursion depth remains at L1, one parameter (w_singleton) is added, no parameters are removed, and the shared prior adds an indicator term for contextually unique singletons lacking duplicates.

name: contextual_contrast_listener
hypothesis: Listeners interpret referring expressions by expecting speakers to refer to the most visually distinctive object in the scene, determined by continuous feature contrast against the other objects in the display. When choosing an object on uninformative prior trials or resolving ambiguous expressions, listeners prefer referents with greater aggregate feature dissimilarity from the surrounding context, treating isolated or contrasting items as salient referents over similar or duplicate items.

name: attentional_crowding_listener
hypothesis: Listeners have limited visual attention, so objects in the visual display compete for attentional processing. Objects that share features with other display items suffer from visual crowding and mutual interference, whereas objects with unique or distinctive features capture visual attention. Pragmatic listeners ground reference resolution in this display-level attentional distribution, biasing choices on both ambiguous and uninformative trials toward referents that escape visual crowding.

name: feature_uncertainty_listener
hypothesis: Listeners interpret referring expressions under uncertainty about which visual feature a speaker intended to name. Rather than assuming a deterministic mapping from words to referential features, listeners entertain the possibility that the speaker's utterance was produced with lexical or transmission noise targeting an alternative feature present in the context. Consequently, reference resolution marginalizes over this latent feature uncertainty, shifting choice probabilities toward referents that possess multiple salient features while softening scalar implicatures.

name: singleton_isolation_l2
hypothesis: We refine singleton_isolation_listener by increasing listener recursive reasoning from depth 1 to depth 2: listeners invert a speaker who simulates a depth-1 pragmatic listener rather than a literal listener, while maintaining the contextual singleton isolation preference as common knowledge across all levels of recursion. This allows listeners to resolve complex scalar implicatures and informativeness asymmetries that depth-1 reasoning leaves ambiguous, while preserving the perceptual isolation bias that favours unique singletons over identical duplicate objects. Compared to singleton_isolation_listener, recursion depth increases from L1 to L2 (choice_probs calls L2 instead of L1), introducing an intermediate pragmatic speaker S2 and depth-2 listener L2 with the singleton prior shared across all levels, with no parameters added or removed (retaining alpha, w_singleton, and lapse).

name: discriminative_singleton_shared_prior
hypothesis: We refine rsa_l1_singleton_shared_prior by incorporating a communicative penalty on ambiguous utterances when distinguishing alternatives exist (taking the discriminative alternative cost component from discriminative_alternative_speaker): speakers incur a production cost when choosing an ambiguous word for their intended referent if a uniquely distinguishing word was available in the visual context. Pragmatic listeners invert this speaker, recognizing that the use of an ambiguous expression signals that the speaker lacked an informative distinguishing alternative, combining Gricean quantity reasoning with shared perceptual singleton and salience grounding. Compared to rsa_l1_singleton_shared_prior, recursion depth remains at L1, one parameter (cost) is added, no parameters are removed, and the speaker choice utility subtracts this communicative penalty for ambiguous words when a distinguishing alternative exists.

Compared to singleton_isolation_listener, recursion depth remains at L1 (choice_probs calls L1), one parameter (w_familiar) is added, no parameters are removed, and the shared prior adds the familiarization base-rate term alongside the singleton isolation indicator.

name: valence_salience_listener
hypothesis: Listeners interpret referring expressions by grounding reference resolution in the speaker's subjective valuation of referents, where referential expectations are driven by perceptual salience (visual feature richness and chromatic prominence) modulated by the speaker's affective valence. In neutral and positive contexts, listeners expect speakers to refer to more salient, feature-rich, or colorful objects; when the speaker specifies a negative attitude ('least favorite'), this evaluative preference reverses, directing expectations toward plain, feature-sparse objects. This shared affective-salience prior guides both prior expectations on uninformative trials and pragmatic reference resolution when hearing a referring expression.

On uninformative trials without an informative word, listeners choose the most visually distinctive object across the entire display.

name: softmax_decision_listener
hypothesis: Listeners compute pragmatic posterior beliefs about the speaker's intended referent, but rather than probability-matching to these beliefs, they apply a softmax decision rule when selecting an object. A decision sensitivity parameter governs the sharpness of this choice, interpolating between probability matching and probability maximizing.

name: oddity_heuristic_listener
hypothesis: Listeners interpret referring expressions using a perceptual oddity heuristic rather than recursive Theory of Mind. When hearing a word that applies to multiple referents, listeners select the contextually unique singleton that lacks identical duplicates in the visual display. On uninformative trials without an informative word, listeners spontaneously choose the unique singleton, and default to uniform choice when no oddity contrast exists.

name: qud_aspect_listener
hypothesis: Listeners interpret referring expressions by modeling speakers as communicating an informative aspect of an object rather than its unique token identity. Speakers select a Question Under Discussion targeting a specific feature of their intended referent and choose words to inform a listener about that aspect. Pragmatic listeners invert this generative process, jointly inferring the speaker's communicative goal and the intended referent upon hearing an utterance.

name: pragmatic_perceptual_mixture_listener
hypothesis: The population of listeners consists of two distinct cognitive types: pragmatic listeners who resolve referring expressions through recursive Theory-of-Mind reasoning about speaker informativeness, and perceptual listeners who select contextually isolated singleton objects that lack identical duplicates. Observed choices reflect a mixture over these two listener types, where pragmatic listeners resolve scalar implicatures while perceptual listeners resolve reference and uninformative prior displays toward salient unique items.

name: entropy_penalized_speaker
hypothesis: Speakers in reference games actively avoid communicative ambiguity by penalizing utterances that leave the listener with high referential uncertainty, measured by the Shannon entropy of the listener's posterior beliefs. Pragmatic listeners invert this ambiguity-averse speaker, resolving referring expressions by expecting speakers to choose words that maximize pragmatic certainty about the intended referent. On uninformative trials without a word, listeners choose uniformly among available objects.

This joint prior penalizes objects that compete for visual processing, capturing perceptual distinctiveness across complex displays while preserving the ability of depth-2 recursive pragmatic reasoning to resolve higher-order scalar implicatures and isolate unique singletons from identical duplicate clones. Compared to singleton_isolation_l2, recursion depth remains at L2 (choice_probs calls L2), one parameter (w_crowd) is added, no parameters are removed (retaining alpha, w_singleton, and lapse), and the shared prior subtracts the exponential feature-crowding term alongside the singleton isolation indicator.

This shared prior grounds depth-2 recursive pragmatic reasoning in visual simplicity, capturing human preferences for minimal referents on uninformative trials and reinforcing scalar implicatures on referring expression trials while preserving second-order Theory of Mind. Compared to singleton_isolation_l2, recursion depth remains at L2 (choice_probs calls L2), one parameter (w_features) is added, no parameters are removed (retaining alpha, w_singleton, and lapse), and the shared prior adds the feature count term alongside the singleton isolation indicator.

This grounds depth-2 recursive pragmatic reasoning in visual chromatic prominence as well as perceptual isolation, accounting for color-based prior expectations while preserving second-order Theory of Mind reasoning over scalar implicatures. Differences from rsa_l2_singleton_shared_prior: recursion depth remains at L2 (choice_probs calls L2); one parameter (w_color) is added; no parameters are removed; and the shared prior adds the chromatic prominence term alongside the singleton isolation indicator, feature count, and familiarization base-rate terms.

name: competitor_confusion_speaker
hypothesis: Speakers avoid choosing referring expressions that are shared with visually similar or confusable distractors in the display, penalizing candidate words by the degree of feature overlap with alternative referents that also satisfy the expression. Pragmatic listeners invert this confusion-averse speaker, expecting speakers to use ambiguous words only when distractors are visually distinct rather than near-identical clones. This disagrees sharply with depth-2 attentional crowding models on displays where an object has high overall visual crowding but possesses an unshared feature: the crowding model penalizes the object globally across all expressions, whereas the competitor-confusion speaker incurs zero penalty when producing the unshared word.

name: competitor_confusability_speaker
hypothesis: Speakers actively minimize competitor confusion: when selecting a referring expression, they penalize words that are shared with contextually similar visual competitors that overlap on unmentioned features. Pragmatic listeners invert this confusion-averse speaker, expecting referring expressions to pick out referents whose competitors are visually distinct rather than confusingly similar.

name: feature_surprisal_listener
hypothesis: Listeners evaluate candidate referents according to the contextual informativeness (Shannon surprisal) of their visual features: contextually rare or unique features carry high information content, whereas ubiquitous features carry low information. Pragmatic listeners ground reference resolution in this feature-surprisal prior, expecting speakers to refer to high-information referents on uninformative trials and when resolving ambiguous referring expressions.

name: bounded_speaker_depth_listener

Specifically, listeners assume the speaker may either be a truthful literal speaker who names any applicable feature of the intended referent, or an informative pragmatic speaker who deliberately selects distinguishing features. Pragmatic reference resolution inverts this generative model of a depth-bounded speaker, balancing literal semantic truth with pragmatic informativeness.

name: evaluative_elaboration_listener

The speaker's communicative framing sets an evaluative stance toward this elaboration: in neutral communication, listeners assume a default positive preference for ornamented referents; an explicit positive framing ('favorite') amplifies this preference, whereas a negative framing ('least favorite') inverts it toward plain, feature-sparse, and desaturated referents. Pragmatic listeners invert a speaker whose referential expectations reflect this evaluative utility, explaining both prior preferences and language-driven choices across framing conditions.

name: rsa_l2_singleton_salience
detail: retired by the cap of 12 live models
hypothesis: We refine rsa_l2_salience by incorporating an isolation preference for contextually unique singletons (taking the singleton isolation component from singleton_isolation_listener) into the listener's referent salience prior: listeners combine depth-2 recursive pragmatic reasoning with a subjective salience prior that favors unique singletons lacking identical duplicates alongside familiar and feature-rich referents, while modeling simulated lower-level agents as reasoning with uniform object priors. This allows listeners to resolve scalar implicatures and capture perceptual singleton isolation and exposure base rates without contaminating lower-level literal and pragmatic reasoning with referent salience. Compared to rsa_l2_salience, recursion depth remains at L2 (choice_probs calls L2), one parameter (w_singleton) is added, no parameters are removed, and the salience prior adds the singleton isolation indicator term alongside feature count and familiarization base rate.
